elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: Total external debt rises from 2,042 in 2015 to 6,540 in 2025. The highest plotted value is in 2025 and the lowest is in 2015.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 2
elements.title: External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations
elements.description: The top bar divides total external debt of 6,540 into public and publicly guaranteed debt of 6,018, private nonguaranteed debt of 60, and short-term debt of 462. A connected bar divides public and publicly guaranteed debt into multilateral creditors, 3,453; bilateral creditors, 1,807; and private creditors, 758. The multilateral bar divides into World Bank-IDA, 845; Islamic Dev. Bank, 611; and other multilateral, 1,997. The bilateral bar divides into China, 1,074; France, 261; and other bilateral, 472; shaded connectors show the relationship between the levels.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four small line charts show external debt and debt service relative to exports and GNI, alongside the shaded 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. The exports-based charts end in 2024 and the GNI-based charts end in 2025. The latest printed ratios range from 45% for external debt / exports to 2% for debt service / GNI.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 3 shows no data values for the exports-based ratios after 2024.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two side-by-side boxes compare official and private creditors. The official creditors box shows maturity of 23 years, a grace period of 5 years, and an interest rate of 2.9%, each above a small indicator bar. The private creditors box shows '..' for maturity, grace period, and interest rate, with empty indicator bars.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
